learning_outcomes.text: Examination of chip removal methods and material behaviors in relation to developing technology, and provision of theoretical knowledge in the manufacturing field.

Ensuring higher quality production by examining the principles of chip removal methods, which play an important role in determining the dimensions and surface quality of machine parts in chip manufacturing. Performing force analyses in chip manufacturing.

syllabus_topics: Principles of chip removal technology
Basic factors affecting chip removal
Study of machining time in lathes
Elastic/plastic deformation and fracture mechanics
Material structures and mechanical behaviors
Examination of economic cutting speed in lathes
Examination of single part cost and tool life
Chip removal mechanics
Factors affecting chip removal
Force analysis and machining time study in milling operations
Motor power and machine selection in milling machines, machine efficiency
Orthogonal and oblique cutting
Introduction to chip removal theories
Friction and drilling torque in drilling operations
Analysis of cutting forces and their effects on tools and machines
Timme model, Ernst and Merchant approaches
Lee and Shafer approaches, Zorev approach
Kinematics of motion transmission mechanisms in machine tools; stepped and stepless mechanisms
Calculation and drawing of setup and revolution speed diagrams
Chip removal models and chip behavior in different materials
Cutting tool geometry
Design of bodies and guides
Stick-slip phenomenon in guides
Cutting tool materials: High-speed steels, polycrystalline Boron Nitrides, diamonds, etc.
Manufacturing of cutting tools, mechanical properties
Effect of cutting forces on guides
Kinematics of motion transmission mechanisms in machine tools
Performance and application areas of cutting tools
